TWZ 获得了有关海狼级潜艇康涅狄格号在 2021 年在南中国海与水下海山相撞后正在进行维修的新细节。海军一直在考虑大约三年的时间表来建造替换的船首声纳导流罩。最终，仅用了不到一年的时间就建成了。康涅狄格州的总体维修计划已被推迟，我们是第一个报告该船预计要到明年夏天才能恢复使用的人。编者注：这篇报道发表后，Janicki Industries 联系我们，要求在进行额外审查时删除圆顶的图像。出于礼貌，我们同意了，如果完全获得批准，我们将重新发布它。 Janicki Industries 今天告诉我们，该公司在大约 10 个月内生产出了新型船首声纳导流罩，并于 2024 年交付给海军。据其网站称，Janicki 拥有为美国核潜艇项目生产“声纳罩和精密加工硬件”的历史。它还支持各种备受瞩目的航空航天项目，包括 B-21 袭击者轰炸机和 F-35 联合攻击战斗机。根据一份经过大量编辑的海军事故报告，康涅狄格号的船头在五年前的碰撞事件发生后，最初至少在某种程度上仍然保持着连接状态。然而，当潜艇一瘸一拐地驶向关岛时，整个船首结构随后断裂。
随后，这艘船驶往加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥，然后前往华盛顿州的普吉特海湾海军造船厂和中间维护设施 (PSNS-IMF)，此后一直待在那里。 2023 年，在普吉特湾海军造船厂和中间维护设施中看到的康涅狄格号航空母舰，其船首圆顶明显缺失。美国海军“普吉特海湾海军造船厂和国际货币基金组织（中间维护设施）需要按照船的计划，在其后面没有生产线的情况下安装一个精密的替换圆顶，”贾尼基在撰写本文时还在其网站上表示。 “Janicki 比次佳选择快了 24 个月，因为工作所需的一切都集中在一个屋檐下：适合半球的 5 轴铣床、证明这一点的计量方法以及形成双曲板的 1,000 吨压力机。”本文顶部的部分图片和下面的完整图片显示了 Janicki 专有的五轴铣床在圆顶上工作的情况。海狼级潜艇艏声纳导流罩的尺寸和复杂性怎么强调都不为过。这些船上的船首声纳阵列直径为 24 英尺。圆顶本身的结构必须按照非常严格的规格建造，以使声纳系统正常工作。海狼级潜艇上的艏声纳阵列，其艏穹顶被拆除。公共领域 过去的五角大楼预算文件和国会拨款法案已经强调了更换康涅狄格州弓形声纳罩的预期成本和复杂性。
2021 年，立法者批准了 1000 万美元专门用于圆顶的资金，以及 4000 万美元用于其他“紧急维修”。全部维修费用仍不得而知，但预计将远高于 5000 万美元。 在 2024 年发布的 2025 财年预算提案中，海军还概述了购买额外船首圆顶的计划，以防其任何一艘“海狼”级潜艇再次遭受类似的严重事故。 “海狼级潜艇的保障战略不包括提供替换潜艇

【原文 English Original】
TWZ has obtained new details about the ongoing repairs to the Seawolf class submarine USS Connecticut following collision with an underwater seamount in the South China Sea in 2021. The Navy had been looking at a roughly three-year timeline for the construction of a replacement bow sonar dome. In the end, it took just under a year for it to be built. The overall schedule for repairs to Connecticut has suffered delays, and we were the first to report that the boat is now not expected to return to service until next summer. Editor’s note: After this story was published, Janicki Industries reached out to us to ask that the image of the dome be taken down while an additional review is conducted. Out of courtesy, we agreed, and we will repost it if and when it is fully approved. Janicki Industries produced the new bow sonar dome in approximately 10 months and delivered it to the Navy in 2024, the company told us today. Janicki has a history of producing “sonar domes and precision machined hardware” for U.S. nuclear submarine programs, according to its website . It has also supported various high-profile aerospace programs, including the B-21 Raider bomber and F-35 Joint Strike Fighter . Connecticut ’s bow had initially remained attached, at least to some degree, following the collision five years ago, according to a heavily redacted Navy report on the accident . However, the entire bow structure subsequently broke away as the submarine limped to Guam . The boat then sailed to San Diego, California , and then to the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS-IMF) in Washington State, where it has been ever since. USS Connecticut seen at the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility in 2023 with its bow dome prominently missing. USN “Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & IMF [Intermediate Maintenance Facility] needed a precision replacement dome with no production line behind it, on the boat’s schedule,” Janicki also says on its website at the time of writing . “Janicki delivered it 24 months faster than the next-best option because everything the job needed sits under one roof: 5-axis mills that fit a hemisphere, the metrology to prove it, and the 1,000-ton press that forms double-curved plate.” The picture seen in part at the top of this story and in full below shows one of Janicki’s proprietary five-axis milling machines at work on the dome. The size and complexity of the bow sonar dome on Seawolf class submarines cannot be overstated. The bow sonar arrays on these boats is 24 feet in diameter. The structure of the dome itself has to be built to very exacting specifications for the sonar system to work properly. A look at the bow sonar array on a Seawolf class submarine with its bow dome removed. Public Domain Past Pentagon budget documents and appropriations bills from Congress had already highlighted the expected costs and complexities of replacing Connecticut ’s bow sonar dome. In 2021, lawmakers approved $10 million in funding specifically for the dome, as well as $40 million for other “emergent repairs.” The full repair bill is still unknown, but is expected to be far steeper than just $50 million. In its Fiscal Year 2025 budget proposal , released in 2024, the Navy also outlined plans to acquire an additional bow dome in case any of its Seawolf class submarines suffered another similarly severe mishap. “The Seawolf Class submarines sustainment strategy did not include the provisioning of replacement bow domes; therefore, no replacement bow domes for these in-service submarines are within the Navy’s inventory,” the budget documents explained. “This program would procure one Seawolf Class bow dome for use in the event replacement is required. Funds in FY25 are to purchase a bow dome which has a three plus year lead time.” Note here the mention of a lead time of at least three years, which is in line with Janicki’s statement that the “next-best option” would have taken two years more to do this work. As TWZ has highlighted in years of reporting now, repairs to Connecticut , in general, were always set to be challenging and costly due to the small size of the Seawolf class and the design being long out of production. The Navy originally planned to acquire 29 of these boats, but ultimately bought just three as a result of post-Cold War drawdowns. In addition, shrinking the program of record so severely caused the unit price of each one to rise substantially, just over $10 billion in 2025 dollars. At the time of writing, they are still the most costly attack submarines ever built. The last of the Seawolf class submarines, the highly secretive USS Jimmy Carter , which entered service in 2005, is also a heavily modified sub-type optimized for underwater espionage missions . USS Connecticut at sea in 2009. USN It is also worth noting that the U.S. Navy, as well as some of its foreign counterparts , have repaired similarly severe damage to submarines by cannibalizing entire sections from decommissioned boats in the same class. However, this is not an option given the size of the Seawolf class and the still very high demand for them operationally . The core design offers advanced capabilities that make even USS Seawolf and USS Connecticut especially well suited to a variety of specialized tasks . This is clearly why the Navy has continued to invest so much in returning Connecticut to the fleet. As mentioned, repairs to Connecticut are now not expected to be finished until sometime in the summer of next year. This is the latest in a succession of schedule slips in recent years. The original goal had been for the boat to be back in service by September 2025. “The Navy’s target completion date for the availability is the summer of 2027. PSNS & IMF is dedicated to executing this work with the highest standards of safety, technical accuracy, and craftsmanship to ensure the ship returns to the fleet ready to take its place at the tip of the spear in defense of our nation’s interests,” a Navy official told TWZ in September. “Current work consists of structural and systems restoration and required lifecycle maintenance.” Earlier in the year, the Navy also revealed that it is now planning on sending Connecticut into retirement in 2031. This means the submarine has just four more years of service ahead of it if the current repair schedule holds. The Navy does have plans to acquire a new class of nuclear attack submarines, currently referred to as SSN(X). In the past, the service has described those future boats as more of a direct successor to the Seawolf class than the versions of the Virginia class it is buying now. A picture of the first-in-class USS Seawolf . USN “The analytical conclusion was unequivocal: to dominate high-end peer threats in the middle of this century, a clean sheet design is required. The Virginia class is a fantastic, unmatched world-class warship, and it will remain the backbone of our attack fleet for decades,” Navy Rear Adm. Andrew Miller said at the Naval Submarine League’s main annual conference last week, per USNI News . “As adversary capabilities evolve, we require expanded payload capacity, greater electrical and hydrodynamic margins and unprecedented architectural flexibility that simply cannot be backfitted into an existing hull form.” Miller is currently the head of the Undersea Warfare Division with the Office of the Chief of Naval Operations. In terms of desired key capabilities for SSN(X), the Navy wants “first, higher flank speed and tactical control speed. Two, improved operational availability. Three, decisive lethality. Four, superior stealth and layered survivability, and finally organic robotic and autonomous systems hosting and command and control,” Miller added. “We are redefining the role of the submarine from a standalone hunter-killer to a capital mothership. By launching uncrewed systems directly from submarine torpedo tubes and integrating unmanned [robotic] vehicles into our battle plans, we dramatically expand the tactical reach of our manned fleet.” The first SSN(X) submarines are not expected to begin entering service until the mid-2040s, at the earliest. The Navy will continue acquiring Virginia class submarines in the interim. This includes stretched Block IV and V versions with Virginia Payload Modules (VPM) that will now be categorized as guided-missile types (SSGN). There will also be a one-of-a-kind seabed warfare version of the Virginia , which could well take over for the USS Jimmy Carter. A briefing slide from General Dynamics Electric Boat detailing existing and future planned subvariants of the Virginia class nuclear submarine. The Block VI and V types have now been reclassified as nuclear-powered guided missile submarines (SSGN) rather than nuclear-powered attack submarines (SSN). General Dynamics Electric Boat When it comes to USS Connecticut , if there are no further delays, the fully repaired submarine with its new bow sonar dome should be back in service by the middle of next year. Chinese v American Views on WAR with Taiwan
Posted Aug 14, 2026 by Martin Armstrong |
The Center for Strategic and International Studies conducted an extraordinary survey of 64 leading experts on China, Taiwan, and cross-Strait relations, including 28 former senior U.S. government officials, 23 former government policy and intelligence analysts, and 13 academics and think-tank experts. What their answers reveal is not that China is preparing to invade Taiwan tomorrow, as the neocons would like everyone to believe, but that Beijing remains willing to wait so long as nobody crosses the line of formal Taiwanese independence. Some 84% said Beijing is willing to wait for unification but will not accept the status quo permanently, while only 10% believed China seeks unification at the earliest opportunity. Not one of the 64 experts believed Beijing would ever accept an independent Taiwan.
This is precisely why Taiwan has become so dangerous. The West keeps portraying the conflict as if Xi Jinping wakes up every morning staring at a calendar trying to decide when to launch an amphibious invasion. Yet 83% of these experts said China did not plan to use significant kinetic force against Taiwan by 2027, and 80% said China’s enormous 2022 military exercises did not indicate Beijing had accelerated its timetable. Only 6% of respondents outside the former senior government group saw 2027 as a hard deadline, while not one former senior U.S. official did. The obsession with 2027 has nevertheless become extremely useful for the military establishment because every supposed deadline becomes another justification for weapons, deployments, bases, and spending.
The survey found that 44% believed Beijing has a hard deadline of 2049, the centennial of the People’s Republic, while 42% believed China could wait indefinitely provided unification remains possible. This is an important distinction because China thinks in terms of generations while Western politicians think in terms of the next election. Beijing does not need to invade Taiwan if economic, political, and military pressure can gradually change the situation in its favor. Only 20% of those surveyed believed China even possessed a coherent roadmap for peaceful unification, which tells us this is not some perfectly scripted invasion plan sitting in Xi’s desk drawer.
Where the numbers become alarming is not an unprovoked invasion but what happens when politicians begin crossing China’s red lines. More than three-quarters of the experts, 77%, believed China would invade within six months if Taiwan formally declared independence. Among former senior U.S. officials, that number was 79%. Even some of those who did not expect an immediate invasion believed Beijing would respond with a blockade or enormous military exercises. This is why politicians encouraging Taiwan toward formal independence are playing with the lives of 23 million people. They can deliver all the speeches they want about democracy from Washington, London, or Brussels, but they will not be the civilians sitting underneath the missiles if their political experiment goes wrong.
Not one expert believed an explicit American commitment to defend Taiwan would cause China to invade immediately, but 64% believed Beijing would respond strongly enough to provoke a U.S.-China or China-Taiwan crisis, while another 31% expected a more limited negative response. Only two of the 64 experts believed formally committing America to Taiwan’s defense would actually deter China from using force because Beijing already assumes that the United States will intervene anyway.
A direct invasion is not even the most likely path toward conflict. Only 8% of the experts described an amphibious invasion within ten years as likely, while 63% called it possible and 27% unlikely. Force short of invasion received much higher probabilities, with 52% saying deliberate escalation such as a blockade was likely or very likely. An accidental military incident was considered even more dangerous, with 34% saying a collision or accident around the Taiwan Strait was likely and another 22% calling it very likely. When warships and aircraft from opposing nuclear powers continually operate around the same small body of water, war does not require some grand master plan. It requires one mistake followed by politicians who refuse to back down.
A later CSIS survey of American and Taiwanese experts reinforces that point. Roughly 90% of U.S. experts and 62% of Taiwanese experts believed China already possessed the capability to impose a law-enforcement-led quarantine that substantially reduces trade into Taiwan. Around 80% of American experts and 60% of Taiwanese experts believed Beijing could execute a PLA blockade, while Taiwanese experts were considerably more skeptical that China could successfully carry out an invasion. If Beijing wanted to coerce Taiwan during the following five years, experts considered a quarantine the most likely option. If China decided it wanted immediate unification, however, approximately 80% regarded a highly kinetic joint blockade as likely or very likely.
This is where the economic consequences become enormous because Taiwan does not need to be invaded for the world economy to be thrown into chaos. A quarantine or blockade would immediately threaten shipping, insurance, semiconductor supply chains, electronics, automobiles, communications equipment, and virtually every modern industry dependent upon advanced chips. The later CSIS survey found most American and Taiwanese experts did not believe Taiwan could withstand a Chinese blockade for longer than three months without substantial U.S. intervention. Washington would then face the decision nobody wants to discuss honestly: accept China’s blockade or attempt to break it militarily and risk direct war between two nuclear powers.
Taiwan is also the world’s semiconductor pressure point. The island’s importance to advanced chip manufacturing means a serious blockade would not remain a regional event. Factories thousands of miles away could discover that a conflict they thought had nothing to do with them suddenly prevents them from obtaining critical components. Markets would begin repricing the risk immediately, shipping premiums would explode, companies would scramble for inventory, and governments would discover once again how fragile global supply chains have become. This is why capital will react long before politicians formally declare that a war has begun.
What I find particularly revealing in the later CSIS survey is the difference between American confidence and Taiwanese confidence in Washington. An astonishing 96% of American experts were completely or moderately confident that the United States would intervene militarily if China invaded Taiwan during the following five years. Taiwanese experts were less confident in American intervention and considerably less confident that U.S. allies would join the fight. It is always easier for people thousands of miles away to be certain about somebody else’s war.
This is precisely why Taiwan remains one of the critical geopolitical pressure points as we move toward 2029. The danger is not simply that China arbitrarily decides to invade. The greater danger is escalation, miscalculation, political promises that cannot be withdrawn, and Western policymakers convincing themselves that every additional provocation somehow produces deterrence. China has made its position on formal independence perfectly clear, and even the experts inside the Western foreign-policy establishment overwhelmingly acknowledge that Beijing would react with force if that line were crossed.
If Taiwan declares formal independence, 77% of the experts surveyed believed China would invade within six months. That is not a statistic policymakers should treat as another war-game scenario. It is a warning about what happens when politicians deliberately remove the ambiguity that has helped keep the peace.

美中經濟暨安全檢討委員會主席薛瑞福（Randall Schriver）。資料照。（宋碧龍／大紀元）
【大紀元2026年11月19日訊】（大紀元記者吳旻洲台灣台北報導）美國國會美中經濟暨安全檢討委員會18日公布年度報告示警，未來24個月將是形塑台海局勢的重要窗口，中共將觀察台灣年底九合一選舉及2028年總統大選結果，評估對台施壓策略，不排除進一步採取隔離、封鎖等行動。
美中經濟暨安全檢討委員會（US-China Economic and Security Review Commission）18日提交國會2026年度報告，其中台灣章節提到，台灣是美國的關鍵夥伴，目前正面臨重要窗口，未來24個月將考驗中共的意志。
報告寫道，中共將視台灣11月底的九合一選舉與2028年的總統選舉結果，評估透過脅迫與政治施壓的手段，是否能讓台灣走向統一，然而絕大多數台灣民眾反對與中共政治融合。
報告還提到，中共黨魁習近平在2028年的軍事實力可能持續增強，但同時也會更缺乏信心，認為只透過政治與經濟的對台施壓等脅迫手段，無法實現統一。這種情勢可能導致中共對台海採取更具侵略性的隔離及封鎖等。
報告還列舉了台灣的兩大重要性，並稱這對美國而言，利害關係從未如此重大。
首先是台灣對於印太地區的權力平衡，由於台灣位於第一島鏈中心位置，鄰接關鍵海上航線，這不僅限制了中共的選擇，同時也增強了美國在印太地區的准入、能力和行動自由。
第二是美國的科技領導地位和經濟安全，報告提到，近年台灣世界領先的半導體產業已成為美國在先進技術領域，特別是人工智慧（AI）領域中保持領先地位的基礎。台灣地位的改變，將改變西太平洋的軍事平衡，考驗美國盟友的信心，並威脅關鍵的技術供應鏈。
報告寫道，中共正試圖透過軍事和海警活動、網絡和資訊作戰、經濟槓桿、法律戰和政治影響力等方式，來削弱台灣的抵抗能力；同時中共也在增強封鎖或入侵台灣的能力。台灣雖然已提高防衛支出，改革軍隊、投資韌性戰力並與美國緊密合作，但仍有弱點。
委員會主席薛瑞福（Randall Schriver）在記者會回應提問時表示，設定24個月為「高風險窗口」，原因是習近平曾對共軍下達命令，要求在2027年必須準備好，加上11月底台灣九合一選舉，與一年多後的總統選舉。
薛瑞福強調，過去台灣選舉顯示，中共會適時升高脅迫，他們會特別關注2028年大選，因為民進黨有可能4度勝選，當然現在不知道結果。
對此，台灣立委王定宇坦言，中共對台灣的野心從來沒有改變過，隨著共軍軍費逐年升高，中共的軍事力量已經嚴重威脅台灣、日本、菲律賓等第一島鏈國家，甚至第二島鏈的澳洲都感到壓力，增加國防預算來強化自我防衛的能力。
不過王定宇也強調，中共升高對台的軍事脅迫，無論台灣哪個政黨執政都一樣，日菲澳也不是由民進黨執政，但是面對中共的軍事脅迫與灰色地帶脅迫也從來沒有減少過，所以跟民進黨是否連任無關。
王定宇表示，這次的報告證明，台灣對美國而言非常具有價值，所以絕不能容許台灣被中共併吞，或者陷入戰爭衝突的威脅當中。因此除非中國共產黨垮台，否則台灣要不斷提高自我防衛力量、強化台灣的國防預算支出、建立與盟友間的合作，才能產生嚇阻力，「這才是真正操之在我的和平之道」。◇

content:
**加利福尼亚州二十九棕榈村** — 从在越南培训公共卫生官员到在印度尼西亚教授食品卫生和疾病预防，分配到海军医学准备和训练司令部 (NMRTC) 二十九棕榈村的一名海军预防医学技术人员在 2026 年太平洋伙伴关系期间帮助加强了国际伙伴关系并保护了部署人员的健康。

一级医院医护兵肖恩·迈克尔·韦默 (Sean Michael Weimer) 是加利福尼亚州莫德斯托人，参加了 2026 年 6 月至 7 月的多国人道主义援助和备灾任务，与美国陆军医疗专家、澳大利亚和印度尼西亚军事人员以及来自多个伙伴国家的公共卫生专业人员合作，分享预防医学实践并降低疾病风险。

对于担任 NMRTC 二十九棕榈村公共卫生局首席士官的韦默来说，这次任务提供了一个机会，可以运用他在环境健康和疾病预防方面的经验，同时与印度太平洋地区的社区建立关系。

韦默说：“太平洋伙伴关系强调了任务准备工作在多大程度上取决于预防疾病发生。” “保持人员健康可以让他们继续工作并支持我们访问的社区。”
韦默于 6 月在越南洞海开始了他的任务，在那里他与美国陆军昆虫学家和微生物学家一起工作，为当地疾病控制中心的越南公共卫生官员提供专门培训。

培训重点是蚊子和蜱虫识别、监测技术和杀虫剂抗药性测试，为参与者提供了监测携带疾病的昆虫和加强当地疾病预防工作的实用知识。

在越南工作结束后，魏默前往菲律宾苏比克湾，在那里登上澳大利亚皇家海军舰艇 HMAS Choules，转机前往印度尼西亚西博尔加。在船上期间，魏默能够与澳大利亚皇家水手一起参加大规模伤亡演习，进一步加深了他的互操作经验。

在整个任务期间，魏默担任预防医学技术员，负责约 150 名人员的部队健康保护。他的职责包括提供食品和水安全、卫生、蚊虫叮咬预防和传染病风险方面的指导。

他还对部署人员进行了有关区域健康威胁的教育，包括疟疾和登革热，强调可以减少疾病并帮助保持行动准备状态的预防措施。

韦默说：“保护团队的健康有助于使任务顺利进行，而培训交流则为我们提供了分享实用技能和相互学习的机会。”
7月，韦默与美国陆军兽医和食品检验员一起在锡博尔加在当地学校、学院、动物农场和屠宰场进行公共卫生培训。

该团队提供了有关食品卫生、正确洗手和畜牧业的指导，分享了减少疾病传播和改善社区健康的实用方法。

【原文 English Original】
**TWENTYNINE PALMS, Calif.** — From training public health officials in Vietnam to teaching food sanitation and disease prevention in Indonesia, a Navy preventive medicine technician assigned to Navy Medicine Readiness and Training Command (NMRTC) Twentynine Palms helped strengthen international partnerships and protect the health of deployed personnel during Pacific Partnership 2026.

Hospital Corpsman 1st Class Sean Michael Weimer, a native of Modesto, California, participated in the multinational humanitarian assistance and disaster preparedness mission from June to July 2026, working alongside U.S. Army medical specialists, Australian and Indonesian military personnel and public health professionals from several partner nations to share preventive medicine practices and reduce the risk of disease.

For Weimer, who serves as the leading petty officer for the directorate for public health at NMRTC Twentynine Palms, the mission offered an opportunity to apply his experience in environmental health and disease prevention while building relationships with communities across the Indo-Pacific.

“Pacific Partnership reinforced how much mission readiness depends on preventing illness before it occurs,” Weimer said. “Keeping personnel healthy allows them to continue their work and support communities we visit.”

Weimer began his mission in June in Dong Hoi, Vietnam, where he worked alongside U.S. Army entomologists and microbiologists to provide specialized training to Vietnamese public health officials at a local disease control center.

The training focused on mosquito and tick identification, surveillance techniques and insecticide resistance testing, providing participants with practical knowledge to monitor disease-carrying insects and strengthen local disease prevention efforts.

Following his work in Vietnam, Weimer traveled to Subic Bay, Philippines, where he boarded the Royal Australian Navy ship HMAS Choules for a transit to Sibolga, Indonesia. During his time aboard, Weimer was able to participate in a mass casualty exercise alongside Royal Australian sailors, furthering his interoperability experience.

Throughout the mission, Weimer served as a preventive medicine technician responsible for force health protection for approximately 150 personnel. His duties included providing guidance on food and water safety, sanitation, mosquito bite prevention and communicable disease risks.

He also educated deployed personnel about regional health threats, including malaria and dengue fever, emphasizing preventive measures that could reduce illness and help sustain operational readiness.

“Protecting the team’s health helped keep the mission on track, while the training exchanges gave us opportunities to share practical skills and learn from one another,” Weimer said.

In July, Weimer joined U.S. Army veterinarians and food inspectors in Sibolga to conduct public health training at local schools, colleges, animal farms and a slaughterhouse.

The team provided instruction on food sanitation, proper handwashing and animal husbandry, sharing practical methods to reduce disease transmission and improve community health.

While the training focused on fundamental preventive medicine practices, Weimer said the opportunity to interact directly with local residents made the experience particularly meaningful.

“Sibolga, Indonesia, stood out to me the most,” Weimer said. “Although the community had limited resources, the people were incredibly friendly, welcoming and happy to have us there.”

Working in schools and other community facilities allowed Weimer and his fellow medical professionals to exchange knowledge with residents while developing relationships that extended beyond the training itself.

“What stayed with me the most was their kindness and enthusiasm,” Weimer said. “It reminded me that building relationships is just as meaningful as the training we provide.”

Collaboration with allied and partner nation personnel was another important aspect of the mission. Working alongside members of the military and public health professionals from different countries exposed Weimer to varying approaches to disease prevention, environmental health and medical readiness.

He said differences in available resources, regional disease threats and the organization of public health services created opportunities for participants to learn from one another.

“Our partners brought valuable knowledge of the diseases and environmental conditions they dealt with regularly,” Weimer said. “We shared our experience with surveillance, standardized procedures and protecting personnel in an operational setting.”

The exchange reinforced the importance of adapting preventive medicine practices to local conditions rather than relying on a single approach.

At NMRTC Twentynine Palms, Weimer oversees 18 environmental health programs supporting Marines, Sailors, staff and beneficiaries across Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center Twentynine Palms.

Those programs include food safety, drinking water surveillance, vector and pest management, immunizations, communicable disease surveillance and sanitation. He also leads and develops hospital corpsmen and preventive medicine technicians, helping prepare personnel to meet operational requirements.

Weimer said his responsibilities at Twentynine Palms provided a foundation for the work he performed overseas, particularly when delivering instruction to audiences with different levels of public health experience.

“My work at NMRTC Twentynine Palms gave me a strong foundation in food safety, water surveillance, sanitation and disease prevention,” Weimer said. “These are areas I work with regularly, so I was able to apply that experience during the mission and explain those practices to different audiences.”

His experience training corpsmen and preventive medicine technicians also helped prepare him to teach at schools, colleges and other facilities throughout the deployment.

Weimer's path to preventive medicine began in a different Navy career field. He originally served as an aviation boatswain's mate before converting to hospital corpsman in search of new professional opportunities.

He eventually pursued preventive medicine because of its emphasis on protecting entire populations rather than focusing exclusively on individual patient care.

“Preventive medicine was a field that really interested me because of its focus on preventing illness and protecting the health of entire groups of people,” Weimer said.

Pacific Partnership 2026 marked Weimer's first humanitarian mission, providing a new perspective on how Navy Medicine personnel can contribute to operational readiness and international cooperation through disease prevention, education and community engagement.

The experience also demonstrated how preventive medicine can serve as a foundation for building trust with partner nations while addressing shared public health challenges.

“In Sibolga, teaching practical skills like food sanitation and handwashing gave us opportunities to connect with the community and build trust,” Weimer said. “Those relationships made the work especially meaningful to me.”

Weimer's contributions during Pacific Partnership 2026 reflect Navy Medicine's commitment to advancing global health, strengthening interoperability with allies and partner nations, and maintaining medical readiness in support of operational missions. These efforts also support the Defense Health Agency's mission to deliver ready medical capabilities to the joint force while strengthening cooperation and improving health outcomes on the global stage.

For other corpsmen and military medical professionals considering participation in future humanitarian missions, Weimer encouraged them to embrace opportunities to work in unfamiliar environments and learn from the people they encounter.

“Go with an open mind, be flexible and willing to learn from your partners and the community,” Weimer said. “Be prepared to adapt what you know to local conditions and available resources.”

Reflecting on his experience, Weimer said the relationships developed during the mission were among its most lasting contributions.

“Take time to get to know the people you are supporting,” Weimer said. “For me, those connections were one of the most rewarding parts of the mission and gave me a broader perspective on what we can accomplish through Navy Medicine.”

Navy Medicine Readiness and Training Command Twentynine Palms operates Defense Health Agency military treatment facility Naval Hospital Twentynine Palms, which delivers safe, high-quality healthcare to service members and their families. The command supports the health and readiness of warfighters at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center Twentynine Palms, the Marine Corps' largest live-fire training installation, while readying Navy Medicine personnel to provide expeditionary medical support around the world.

content:
关岛阿加纳高地——美国海军医疗准备和训练司令部 (USNMRTC) 关岛的一支远征医疗队最近在亚伯拉罕·林肯号航空母舰 (CVN 72) 上部署后返回家园。

重症监护护士 Jose Tolentino 中尉和飞行途中护理兼一般值勤护理人员一等医院医护员 Luis Nazareno 组成了途中护理系统 (ERCS) 3 团队。他们的主要任务是为医疗后送提供先进的医疗能力，同时完全融入船舶的日常医疗运营。

托伦蒂诺说：“对于 ERCS 团队来说，典型的一天首先是确保设备和物资准备就绪，以防我们需要进行医疗后送。” “我们支持早晨病假电话、飞行甲板战斗更衣站值班、晚上病假电话以及全天出现的任何医疗紧急情况。”

纳扎雷诺是一位经验丰富的水手，正在进行第九次部署并具备全套资格，他指出该团队很快就成为了船舶节奏的一部分。纳扎雷诺从第一天起就担任导师并担任值班部门负责人。他的经验和资历使他能够立即担任关键的值班职务。他报到后不久就帮助驾驶舱战备站值班，值班时间超过1000小时，保障了驾驶舱人员的安全。
“我们很容易融入船舶的运营，”纳扎雷诺说。 “每当他们需要帮助时，我们都会很乐意在等待他们执行主要医疗后送任务时提供帮助。”

他们的资格也转化为船舶的整体医疗准备情况。 Tolentino 担任林肯美国红十字会生命支持项目 (CPR/BLS) 的项目经理，领导 21 名讲师并管理 82 个生命支持课程。

纳扎雷诺在数百名水手成功获得心肺复苏和战术战斗伤亡护理 (TCCC) 认证方面发挥了至关重要的作用。托伦蒂诺还担任战术战斗伤亡护理教练。这些努力显着增加了船上能够有效应对医疗紧急情况的水兵人数。

该小组还在部署期间进行了多次医疗后送，包括拯救一名呼吸困难的平民渔民。

纳扎雷诺描述了另一个复杂的案例，涉及四辆不同车辆和人员之间的协调转移。

“这确实证明了美国海军的灵活性和后勤协调性，”他说。

此次部署强化了有关手术医学的几个关键经验教训，这些经验教训直接影响了团队如何照顾水手和支持船舶。在海上，他们必须足智多谋，在物资有限的情况下做出决定，并跳出框框思考。
“手术医学确实与医院环境‘相同但不同’，”纳扎雷诺解释道。 “药物本质上是一样的，但演示和执行可能需要开箱即用的思维。”

托伦蒂诺表示同意并表示：“我学会了如何利用船上有限的资源来提供护理，以及为面临后勤挑战的时期做好计划的重要性。”

尽管船上生活有独特的限制，这些课程使团队能够为船上的水手提供有效的护理和培训。

与全船各个部门的水手一起工作留下了持久的印象。

【原文 English Original】
AGANA HEIGHTS, GUAM – An Expeditionary Medicine team from U.S. Navy Medicine Readiness and Training Command (USNMRTC) Guam recently returned home after deploying aboard the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN 72).

Lt. Jose Tolentino, a critical care nurse, and Hospital Corpsman 1st Class Luis Nazareno, a flight enroute care and general duty corpsman, formed the En Route Care System (ERCS) 3 team. Their primary mission was to deliver advanced medical capability for medical evacuations while integrating fully into the ship’s daily medical operations.

“A typical day for the ERCS team began with ensuring equipment and supplies were ready in case we were called upon for a medevac,” Tolentino said. “We supported morning sick call, flight deck battle dressing station watch, evening sick call, and any medical emergencies that arose throughout the day.”

Nazareno, a seasoned Sailor on his ninth deployment and the full set of qualifications, noted the team quickly became part of the ship’s rhythm. Nazareno served as a mentor and assumed the role of duty section lead from day one. His experience and qualifications allowed him to step into critical watch standing roles immediately. He helped stand the flight deck battle dressing station watch shortly after reporting aboard and stood more than 1,000 hours of watch, ensuring the safety of flight deck personnel.

“We integrated into the ship’s operations easily,” Nazareno said. “Whenever they needed help, we gladly offered while we waited to be utilized for our primary medevac mission.”

Their qualifications also translated into the ship’s overall medical readiness. Tolentino assumed the role of program manager for Lincoln’s American Red Cross Life Support Programs (CPR/BLS, leading 21 instructors and managing 82 life support classes.

Nazareno played a vital role in the successful certification of hundreds of Sailors in CPR and Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC). Tolentino also served as a Tactical Combat Casualty Care instructor. These efforts significantly expanded the number of Sailors aboard who could respond effectively to medical emergencies.

The team also conducted several medevacs during the deployment, including saving a civilian fisherman in respiratory distress.

Nazareno described another complex case involving coordinated transfers across four different vehicles and crews.

“It was really a testament to the flexibility and logistical coordination of the U.S. Navy,” he said.

The deployment reinforced several key lessons about operational medicine that directly shaped how the team cared for Sailors and supported the ship. At sea, they had to be resourceful, make decisions with limited supplies, and think outside the box.

“Operational medicine really is ‘same but different’ from the hospital setting,” Nazareno explained. “The medicine is fundamentally the same, but the presentation and execution may need out-of-the-box thinking.”

Tolentino agreed and said, “I learned how to use the limited resources aboard a ship to provide care and the importance of planning for periods with logistical challenges.”

These lessons enabled the team to deliver effective care and training to the Sailors aboard the ship, despite the unique constraints of shipboard life.

Working alongside Sailors from every department throughout the ship left a lasting impression.

“Every department plays a critical role in ensuring a successful deployment, from the culinary specialists providing meals to the damage controlmen troubleshooting equipment,” Tolentino said.

Nazareno added that the Lincoln’s crew welcomed them with open arms.

For Tolentino, it was his first shipboard deployment. He relied heavily on Nazareno’s extensive experience and the ship’s hospital corpsmen who taught him the nuances of shipboard patient care, charting, and working across medical departments from radiology to the laboratory.

Morale remained high through shipboard programs. Wi-Fi allowed Sailors to stay connected with family. The ship’s Morale, Welfare and Recreation team, known as the “Fun Boss,” organized talent shows, dance lessons, and painting events, while the “Fit Boss” led fitness challenges, run club, and high-intensity interval training classes.

Life at sea also brought challenges, including delay in receiving mail and limited workout spaces. Nazareno simply observed, “You really can survive without your personal electronics.”

The deployment tested their resilience when the original return date slipped repeatedly into the summer.

“I learned to become more fluid and not focus on things outside my control,” Tolentino said.

Nazareno agreed. “Not knowing when the finish line was a challenge. However, by being positive and focusing on the tasks at hand, long deployments become easier.”

When the ship finally approached Guam, the reality of homecoming set in.

“It seemed unreal,” Tolentino said. “I still didn’t believe we were coming home until we were actually days out from Guam.”

Nazareno summed up with a seasoned Sailor’s perspective.

“Port isn’t real until feet are on the ground.”

Reuniting with family brought powerful moments. Tolentino’s 12-year-old son cried upon seeing him on the pier. Both expressed deep gratitude for the support they received from USNMRTC Guam.

“The command acted and responded promptly whenever I reached out,” Tolentino said. “My spouse works in the hospital laboratory, and her leadership helped manage her schedule and workload while she held things down at home. Leadership from the hospital and the Emergency Department even met us on the pier on a weekend. That gesture brought real meaning to the word ‘family."

Nazareno echoed the appreciation.

“Every bit of administrative and logistical support made our lives easier and allowed us to focus on the mission,” Nazareno said. “And the coffee that was sent really was a lifesaver in the early months.”

For the command’s leadership, the successful deployment of the ERCS team represents the real-world application of the Expeditionary Medicine readiness capabilities.

“The entire command is very proud that our own Lt. Tolentino and Hospital Corpsman 1st Class Nazareno supported the USS Abraham Lincoln deployment,” said Captain James Demitrack, commanding officer of USNTRC Guam. “Our command is responsible for eight Expeditionary Medicine platforms, and these units help to make us who we are. The complex patient care that our providers, nurses and corpsmen provide at our hospital supports the readiness of these teams. The presence of these teams here in Guam makes it clear to all of our staff that our command is critical to the operational readiness of the entire Navy.”

Both Sailors return with valuable experience they intend to share with their command — practical medevac expertise, greater flexibility, and the knowledge that an upbeat attitude makes even the longest deployments more manageable.

U.S. Navy Medicine Readiness and Training Command Guam directly sustains Navy and Marine Corps operational readiness, preparing its medical forces to deliver critical medical support to maritime and expeditionary forces, ashore or at sea, anytime and anywhere.

content:
2026年11月19日，在深圳麒麟山莊，中共黨魁習近平、美國總統川普和俄羅斯總統普京在APEC峰會期間舉行三方會晤。安保人員在會面地點外站崗。(Greg Baker/AFP)
【大紀元2026年11月19日訊】（大紀元記者張婷綜合報導）週四（11月19日），一名美國記者因在川習會期間提出英偉達創辦人黃仁勳和疑似中共女間諜有染有關的敏感問題，而被中共官員禁止進入隨後召開的美中俄三邊會議。儘管白宮在事件發生後努力爭取讓該記者進入會場，但中共官員仍堅持將其排除在外。川普（特朗普）總統對這次訪問期間記者權限受限表示遺憾。
週四，美國總統川普和中共黨魁習近平舉行雙邊會晤期間，白宮隨行記者團中的彭博社首席政治記者安瑪麗‧霍登（Annmarie Hordern）提出問題，針對英偉達前首席執行官黃仁勳與疑似中共間諜的中國女子黃樂之間的婚外情一事，尋求川普總統的置評。美國情報界有人認為黃樂是中共國家安全部直接招募的人員，負責搜集黃仁勳的情報，藉此掌握美國AI芯片動態。黃仁勳事件隨即上升為美國國安事件。
「川普總統，黃仁勳是否對美國不忠？」霍登在川習會期間提問道。
白宮隨行記者團說，隨後另一名記者也試圖提問，但遭到中共官員「噓聲制止」。
在隨後舉行的美中俄三國領導人會議上，霍登被告知不得入場。中方的理由是，大聲喊出問題被視為極不禮貌的行為，如果再有此類舉動，相關人員將被帶出會場。
一位白宮官員表示，儘管白宮方面極力爭取讓該記者進入現場，但中方堅持拒絕其入內。
福克斯新聞頻道（Fox News Channel）白宮資深記者、白宮記者協會主席雅基‧海因里希（Jacqui Heinrich）在社交媒體平台X上說，白宮積極爭取讓記者進入的做法值得讚揚。
川普總統表示，他和習近平簡短地提到了黃仁勳的事情。
白宮記者協會主席海因里希說，在週四早些時候的雙邊會晤中，川普總統對此次訪問中媒體進入現場採訪報導受到限制表示遺憾。
據福克斯新聞報導，峰會期間，中共官員對白宮隨行記者團施加嚴格限制，包括限定記者可以拍攝及傳送哪些活動環節的畫面。
川普說：「媒體沒能看到其中的一些場面，實在太可惜了。」
川普與中俄兩國領導人之間的峰會經過了精心編排；峰會舉辦地深圳也處於嚴密的安保之下。長期以來，在中國進行報導的媒體記者不僅面臨來自官方的敵意，在試圖提問或採訪活動時，還受到嚴格的限制。
川普在今年5月份訪華期間，與習近平在北京會晤時，美國特勤局人員曾與中方官員發生衝突。當川普和習近平造訪北京天壇時，記者們被拒之門外。當時媒體報導說，由於美中官員之間進行了長時間且愈發激烈的交涉，隨行記者團進入天壇景區的行程被耽擱了近半個小時。

content:
发言人办公室 美国参加2026年东亚峰会情况介绍 2026年11月18日 在11月17日于菲律宾马尼拉举行的东亚峰会上，美国重申对自由开放印太的承诺，表示支持东盟中心地位，并强调美国是该地区首选的能源和技术伙伴。为了在美国-东盟关系成立50周年之前推进全面战略伙伴关系，美国和东盟通过了《实施美国-东盟领导人共同愿景声明的综合工作计划，以促进东盟和美国更强大、更安全和更繁荣》（2026-2030年）。美国强调其与盟友和伙伴一道致力于加强威慑，以维护印太地区的和平与稳定。在两国建交80周年之际，美国祝贺菲律宾成功担任东盟轮值主席国。促进和平，加强自由开放的印太地区 美国将继续在印太地区发挥领导作用，并威慑该地区任何试图通过武力解决争端的国家，这体现了特朗普总统通过实力实现和平的承诺。
美国将继续维护《联合国海洋法公约》所反映的国际法规定的所有国家行使航行和飞越自由的权利，包括在南中国海。台海的和平与稳定对于印太地区的安全与繁荣仍然至关重要，美国反对任何单方面改变现状的行为。美国仍然致力于实现朝鲜完全无核化，并全面执行联合国安理会所有涉朝决议。扩大贸易、能源和技术联系美国仍然是东盟最大的单一国家外国直接投资者，截至 2025 年，该地区的外国直接投资超过 5,570 亿美元，为美国提供了约 532,000 个就业岗位。美国祝贺东盟领导人签署《数字经济框架协议》，该协议有可能为美国科技公司提供更大的机会，让该地区的数字经济到2030年将达到2万亿美元。随着美国超级智能（SI）技术在全球树立黄金标准，美国正在与东南亚伙伴合作，扩大获得美国技术的机会，包括通过美国-东盟SI SPARK计划，这将有助于释放该地区的经济潜力。
通过签署《人工智能机会声明》，越南和柬埔寨与其他国家一道致力于促进基于可信赖伙伴关系的创新。为了支持该地区的人工智能准备工作，美国将与印度尼西亚政府、东盟秘书处和卡内基梅隆大学合作，于 12 月在雅加达举办东盟人工智能周。美国和菲律宾签署了一项为期五年的经济繁荣和韧性战略目标协议，该协议将动员对包括吕宋经济走廊在内的关键基础设施的投资，并与可靠的合作伙伴一起确保供应链的安全。作为世界上最大的能源生产国之一，美国可以为东南亚几代人的增长提供动力。美国准备与东盟合作加强该地区的能源安全

Office of the Spokesman The United States’ Participation in the 2026 East Asia Summit Fact Sheet November 18, 2026 At the East Asia Summit in Manila, Philippines on November 17, the United States reaffirmed its commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific, expressed support for ASEAN centrality, and underscored the United States as the region’s preferred partner for energy and technology. To advance their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership ahead of the 50 th anniversary of U.S.-ASEAN relations, the United States and ASEAN adopted the Comprehensive Work Plan to Implement the U.S.-ASEAN Leaders’ Joint Vision Statement to Promote a Stronger, Safer, and More Prosperous ASEAN and America (2026-2030). The United States highlighted its commitment, with allies and partners, to strengthen deterrence to safeguard peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region. The United States congratulated the Philippines on a successful ASEAN chair year, as the two countries mark 80 years of diplomatic relations. Promoting Peace and Strengthening a Free and Open Indo-Pacific Reflecting President Trump’s commitment to peace through strength, the United States will continue to lead in the Indo-Pacific and deter any nation in the region tempted to settle disputes by force. The United States will continue to uphold the right of all nations under international law as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Seas (UNCLOS) to exercise freedom of navigation and overflight, including in the South China Sea. Peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait remain essential to the security and prosperity of the Indo-Pacific and the United States opposes any unilateral change to the status quo. The United States remains committed to the complete denuclearization of the DPRK and the full implementation of all DPRK-related UN Security Council resolutions. Expanding Trade, Energy, and Technology Ties The United States remains ASEAN’s largest single country foreign direct investor, with more than $557 billion in foreign direct investment in the region as of 2025, which supports an estimated 532,000 American jobs. The United States congratulated ASEAN leaders for signing the Digital Economy Framework Agreement, which has the potential to provide U.S. technology companies with greater opportunities in the region’s digital economy projected to reach $2 trillion by 2030. As American Super Intelligence (SI) technology sets the gold standard worldwide, the United States is working with Southeast Asian partners to expand access to U.S. technology, including through the U.S.-ASEAN SI SPARK program, which will help unlock the region’s economic potential. By signing the AI Opportunity Statement, Vietnam and Cambodia joined other nations in committing to fostering innovation anchored in trusted partnerships. To support the region’s SI readiness, the United States will collaborate with the Government of Indonesia, ASEAN Secretariat, and Carnegie Mellon University to host ASEAN SI Week in Jakarta in December. The United States and the Philippines signed a five-year Economic Prosperity and Resilience Strategic Objective Agreement, which will mobilize investment in critical infrastructure, including in the Luzon Economic Corridor, and secure supply chains with reliable partners. As one of the world’s largest energy producers, the United States can power Southeast Asia’s growth for generations. The United States is ready to work with ASEAN to strengthen the region’s energy security through support for the ASEAN Power Grid. The United States is sharing its 70 years of experience and leadership in nuclear energy by promoting nuclear safety, security, and nonproliferation in Southeast Asia. Building on our existing 123 Agreements with Indonesia and Vietnam, the United States has entered into 123 Agreements with the Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand, and launched negotiations with Malaysia. This cooperation will help the region meet its growing energy demand, including reliable power for SI. The United States is expanding civil nuclear cooperation in Southeast Asia, where energy demand is anticipated to triple by 2050. Consistent with the U.S.-Japan-South Korea Memorandum of Cooperation (MOC) on Small Modular Reactor (SMR) deployments, the United States is providing SMR control room simulators and other technical assistance to Indonesia under the Department’s Foundational Infrastructure for the Responsible Use of Small Modular Reactor Technology (FIRST) program to help establish Indonesia as a regional SMR hub. These partnerships strengthen energy security, drive economic growth, and support jobs in the United States and across the region. Combating Scams and Transnational Crime Scam groups based in Southeast Asia stole at least $18.2 billion from Americans and around $23 billion from citizens of ASEAN member states in 2025. In response, President Trump issued Executive Order 14390, titled “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” and the Department of State has confronted these criminal groups head on. The Department is directing an additional $26.2 million to train and equip Southeast Asian law enforcement and criminal justice officials to work with U.S. law enforcement to catch and prosecute scam network operators. The United States and 12 regional partners in the Contact Group to Counter Criminal Online Scams agreed to a Statement of Principles to drive joint action to dismantle the scam syndicates targeting our people. The United States and ASEAN also adopted the U.S.-ASEAN Statement on 10 Public-Private Partnership Principles for Tackling Online Scams, deepening regional and private-sector cooperation.

乐天证券紧急应对数据泄露事件
周一，乐天证券检测到未经授权访问的可能性。后来发现其测试环境系统中存储的数据可能已向外泄露。 |路透社

乐天证券正在迅速努力解决最近因未经授权的访问而导致的大规模数据泄露问题。
针对数据泄露事件，这家在线证券公司周四宣布，将推迟下周在东京涩谷区开设实体店与客户进行面对面咨询的计划。
该公司还决定暂时免除向其他金融机构转让投资信托持股的费用。
此次数据泄露引发了对该公司信息管理系统的质疑。
周一，乐天证券检测到未经授权访问的可能性。后来发现其测试环境系统中存储的数据可能已向外泄露。
多达1572万个账户可能受到该事件的影响，其中约447万个账户包含个人信息，包括姓名、出生日期、地址、年收入水平和金融资产。
在测试环境中，公司通常使用虚拟信息。不过，这次包含了实际的客户信息。
“本案与以往不同，客户金融资产等高度敏感信息被泄露。”某大型券商高管表示。
静冈大学名誉教授、金融信息系统专家Masayuki Endo表示：“使用实际数据进行测试可以有效防止系统故障。”
然而，远藤指出需要加强测试环境中的网络安全措施，例如测试后迅速删除数据。

On Monday, Rakuten Securities detected the possibility of unauthorized access. It later found that data stored in its test environment system may have leaked externally. | REUTERS

Rakuten Securities is working quickly to address a recent massive data breach caused by unauthorized access.
In response to the data breach, the online securities firm announced Thursday that it will postpone a plan to open a brick-and-mortar store for face-to-face consultations with customers in Tokyo’s Shibuya district next week.
The company has also decided to temporarily waive fees for transferring investment trust holdings to other financial institutions.
The data breach has raised questions about the company’s information management system.
On Monday, Rakuten Securities detected the possibility of unauthorized access. It later found that data stored in its test environment system may have leaked externally.
Up to 15.72 million accounts were potentially affected by the incident, and about 4.47 million of them contained personal information, including names, dates of birth, addresses, annual income levels and financial assets.
In the test environment, the company usually uses dummy information. However, actual customer information was included this time.
“This case is different from previous ones in that highly sensitive information, such as customers’ financial assets, has been breached,” said a senior official of a major brokerage firm.
Masayuki Endo, professor emeritus at Shizuoka University and an expert on financial information systems, said, “Tests using actual data are effective in preventing system failures.”
However, Endo noted the need to strengthen cybersecurity measures in test environments, such as swiftly deleting data after tests.

台北，11 月 19 日 - 台湾国防部表示，两架俄罗斯军用 Tu-95 飞机周四从南部接近后飞越台湾东部，这是本周第二次报告看到此类活动，并且几乎肯定是从越南飞回来的。
这些航班起飞之际，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京正在中国南部的深圳参加亚太经合组织峰会，他还将在那里与中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普举行三边会议。
自2022年俄罗斯入侵乌克兰以来，主要半导体生产商台湾已与西方国家一起对俄罗斯实施广泛的经济制裁。
中国军队每天都在台湾周边活动。
中国将台湾视为自己的领土，俄罗斯一再支持这一立场。台湾政府拒绝北京的主权主张，称只有台湾人民才能决定他们的未来。
台湾国防部表示，两架被北约称为“熊”的Tu-95进入台湾防空识别区，然后离开台湾周围空域，飞向台湾东北部港口城市基隆附近。
该部公布了其中一架飞机的照片，据称是从一架台湾 F-16 战斗机上拍摄的。
虽然路透社无法独立核实该图像的日期和位置，但其尾部的注册号与本周周二和周三在越南岘港看到的一架飞机相符。
周四早些时候发布的社交媒体视频显示，这架飞机从岘港机场起飞，并得到了路透社的证实。
台湾国防部在一份简短声明中表示，台湾武装部队使用联合情报、监视和侦察手段来监控活动的整个过程，并“做出适当反应”。
台湾周二表示，两架俄罗斯军用飞机从台湾东海岸向南飞行。日本当天也报告了同样的活动，并公布了一张显示飞机在台湾东海岸飞行的地图。
采用老化的冷战时代设计，一些 Tu-95 可以携带核武器，但其他类型则用于远程监视和侦察。
俄罗斯国防部尚未回应置评请求。
周四早些时候，台湾亚太经合组织峰会特使、电脑制造商宏碁创始人施振荣在峰会开始时与普京短暂握手。路透社

Published Nov 19, 2026, 03:10 PM
Updated Nov 19, 2026, 06:25 PM
TAIPEI, Nov 19 - Taiwan's defence ministry said that two Russian military Tu-95 aircraft flew past the island's east on Thursday after approaching from the south, the second time this week it has reported seeing such activity and almost certainly flying back from Vietnam.
The flights have come as Russian President Vladimir Putin is in Shenzhen, in southern China, for the APEC summit, where he will also hold a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump.
Major semiconductor producer Taiwan has joined Western countries in placing wide economic sanctions on Russia since it invaded Ukraine in 2022.
China's military operates around Taiwan on a daily basis.
China views Taiwan as its own territory, a position Russia has repeatedly backed. Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, saying only the island's people can decide their future.
The Taiwanese defence ministry said the two Tu-95s, known by NATO as "Bears", entered Taiwan's Air Defence Identification Zone, then exited airspace around Taiwan to the island's northeast, off the port city of Keelung.
The ministry published a picture of one of the aircraft it said was taken from a Taiwanese F-16 fighter.
While Reuters could not independently verify the date and location of that image, the registration number on its tail matched an aircraft seen in Vietnam's Da Nang on Tuesday and Wednesday this week.
The aircraft was seen taking off from Da Nang airport in social media footage released on early on Thursday and verified by Reuters.
Taiwan's armed forces used joint intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance means to monitor the full course of the activity and "responded appropriately", the ministry said in a short statement.
Taiwan said on Tuesday two Russian military aircraft had flown in a southerly direction down its east coast. Japan also reported the same activity that day and published a map showing the aircraft flying down Taiwan's east coast.
An ageing Cold War-era design, some Tu-95s can carry nuclear weapons but others of that type are used for long-range surveillance and reconnaissance.
Russia's defence ministry has not responded to requests for comment.
Earlier on Thursday, Taiwan's envoy to the APEC summit, Stan Shih, the founder of computer maker Acer, briefly shook hands with Putin at the start of the summit. REUTERS

zh_title: 随着俄罗斯和中国的逼近，美国加大了向最西端岛链的兵力投射
summary: 美国空军正在加强在该国最西端岛屿的训练，寻求开发更多的地方来投射力量并监视太平洋和北极的对手。这些努力在十月下旬就可见一斑，当时空军部署到阿拉斯加阿留申群岛的谢米亚岛进行一次罕见的演习，空军发布了一份概述其在关岛附近岛屿行动计划的提案。在比阿拉斯加大陆更靠近俄罗斯的谢米亚，10 月 18 日至 26 日期间，F-16、加油机和货机部署到埃尔克森机场。
content:
美国空军正在加强在该国最西端岛屿的训练，寻求开发更多的地方来投射力量并监视太平洋和北极的对手。这些努力在十月下旬就可见一斑，当时空军部署到阿拉斯加阿留申群岛的谢米亚岛进行一次罕见的演习，空军发布了一份概述其在关岛附近岛屿行动计划的提案。谢米亚距离俄罗斯比阿拉斯加大陆更近，10 月 18 日至 26 日期间，F-16、加油机和货机部署到厄里克森机场。在那里，这些喷气式飞机“保持警惕”，机组人员就位，随时准备在接到通知后立即起飞。阿拉斯加 NORAD 地区发言人 Kitsana Dounglomchan 上尉在一封电子邮件中表示：“虽然飞机在 20 世纪 80 年代处于警戒状态是很常见的事情，但这次部署标志着数十年来飞机在厄尔克森首次处于警戒状态。”作为美加国土防御演习的一部分，谢米亚部署以远程行动结束。当 F-16 战机从厄尔克森起飞，覆盖阿拉斯加战区南部时，位于西边 1,600 英里的艾尔森空军基地的 F-35 和 F-16 战机也起飞，覆盖战区西北部。加拿大 CF-18 飞机从距谢米亚 2,600 英里的冷湖基地起飞，覆盖北部地区。
阿拉斯加北美防空司令部司令、空军中将罗伯特·戴维斯在一份新闻稿中表示，从厄尔克森出发的行动“证明我们可以部署到严峻的地点，保持警戒，在短时间内发射，并无缝整合美国和加拿大军队以保卫北方通道”。自二战以来，美国军方一直在谢米亚地区活跃。冷战期间，该基地驻有加油机和侦察机以及雷达来监视苏联的活动，特别是苏联的洲际弹道导弹。大型 Cobra Dane 雷达建于 20 世纪 70 年代，至今仍用于监测导弹活动。最近在谢米亚的部署突显了其作为阿留申群岛栖息地的持续重要性，阿留申群岛横跨连接太平洋和北极的战略重要水域。 2024 年 9 月，美国士兵使用 HIMARS 发射器进行了一次“兵力投送行动”，此前俄罗斯和中国在该地区进行了一系列活动，其中包括中俄轰炸机在阿拉斯加附近进行的首次巡逻。最近的其他演习似乎侧重于保护该岛的基础设施免受海上入侵和空袭。据一份新闻稿称，在厄里克森期间，飞行员还认证了该基地的飞机拦截系统，可以处理 F-16 战斗机，“进一步验证了厄里克森机场作为未来战斗机在严峻机场执行任务的可行地点”。
Dounglomchan拒绝就厄尔克森的未来行动发表评论，但表示北美防空司令部保持着“作战能力”，可以“在我们选择的时间和地点”在阿拉斯加和北极周围调动部队，并且“经常到厄尔克森这样的偏远地区”。随着谢米亚演习的结束，空军分享了未来在太平洋中部岛屿上的行动计划。 在 10 月底发布的一份提案中，空军表示将研究每年在北马里亚纳群岛联邦罗塔岛、塞班岛和天宁岛的机场进行多达 1,500 次甚至可能超过 1,800 次飞机行动（例如起飞和降落）的影响。这些作业将是小型、中型和大型演习的一部分

【原文 English Original】
The U.S. Air Force is stepping up its training on the country’s westernmost islands as it seeks to develop more places from which to project power and monitor adversaries across the Pacific and the Arctic. Those efforts were visible in late October, when airmen deployed to Shemya Island in Alaska’s Aleutian Islands for a rare exercise, and when the Air Force released a proposal outlining its plans for operations on islands near Guam. On Shemya, which is closer to Russia than to mainland Alaska , F-16s, tankers and cargo planes deployed to Eareckson Air Station from Oct. 18 to Oct. 26. While there, the jets “sat alert,” with crews in position and maintaining readiness to launch on short notice. “While it was commonplace for aircraft to sit alert in the 1980s, this deployment marks the first time in decades that aircraft have sat alert at Eareckson,” Capt. Kitsana Dounglomchan, Alaskan NORAD Region spokesperson, said in an email. The Shemya deployment ended with long-range operations as part of a U.S.-Canada homeland-defense exercise. As F-16s launched from Eareckson to cover the southern portion of the Alaska theater of operations, F-35s and F-16s at Eielson Air Force Base 1,600 miles to the west took off to cover the northwest portion of the theater. Canadian CF-18s flew from their base at Cold Lake, 2,600 miles from Shemya, to cover the northern part. Operating from Eareckson “proved we can deploy to an austere location, maintain alert, launch on short notice, and seamlessly integrate U.S. and Canadian forces to defend the northern approaches,” Air Force Lt. Gen. Robert Davis, commander of the Alaskan NORAD region, said in a press release. The U.S. military has been active on Shemya since World War II. During the Cold War, the base hosted refueling and surveillance aircraft as well as radars to monitor Soviet activity, especially Soviet ICBMs. The massive Cobra Dane radar was built there in the 1970s and is still used to monitor missile activity. Recent deployments to Shemya underscore its continued relevance as a perch in the Aleutians, which stretch across strategically important waters linking the Pacific and Arctic. A “ force projection operation ” by U.S. soldiers with HIMARS launchers in September 2024 came after a flurry of Russian and Chinese activity in the area, including the first Sino-Russian bomber patrol near Alaska. Other recent exercises appear to have focused on defending the island’s infrastructure from seaborne incursions and aerial attacks. While at Eareckson, airmen also certified the base’s aircraft-arresting system to handle F-16s, “further validating Eareckson Air Station as a viable location for future fighter operations from an austere airfield,” according to a press release. Dounglomchan declined to comment on future operations at Eareckson but said NORAD maintains “the operational capability” to move forces around Alaska and the Arctic “at a time and place of our choosing” and “oftentimes to remote locations like Eareckson.” As the drills on Shemya wrapped up, the Air Force shared its plans for future operations on islands in the central Pacific. In a proposal released at the end of October, the service said it would study the impact of conducting up to 1,500 and potentially more than 1,800 aircraft operations, such as takeoffs and landings, annually at airfields on Rota, Saipan, and Tinian in the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. The operations would be part of small, medium and large drills held several times a year for a few weeks at a time. They would also involve deployment of up to 550,000 gallons of fuel and up to 1,000 personnel at each airfield, as well as munitions, temporary infrastructure, and support operations. The Air Force said its study would assess “the potential social, economic, and environmental effects” of those operations. HC-130J Combat King II pilots assigned to the 211th Rescue Squadron pilot an aircraft en route from Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson to Eareckson Air Station, Alaska, on Oct. 19, 2026. (Airman 1st Class Frank Houseton/U.S. Air Force) The study won’t be completed until mid-2028, but the proposal highlights the Air Force’s recent focus on those islands, especially Tinian, where airmen are refurbishing North Field , one of the U.S.’s largest and most important WWII airbases. North Field was abandoned and overgrown after the war, but airmen have been clearing vegetation, removing debris and rehabilitating runways since late 2023. That work is ongoing but had progressed enough by mid-2025 for North Field to be deemed “a semi-permanent [contingency] location” for the Air Force’s main base on Guam, about 100 miles to the south. The Northern Marianas is a U.S. territory in the Second Island Chain, which stretches from Japan through the central Pacific to Indonesia. The Air Force has been scouting airfields in that island chain and conducting renovations and upgrades to make them better able to support its Agile Combat Employment concept, which emphasizes dispersal and resilience to counter the threat from China. “China’s missile force is large, but it’s not unlimited. Every additional airfield from where the Air Force can operate is another of targets China has to cover. That’s the logic behind Agile Combat Employment,” said Kelly Greico, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center. Improvements on Shemya and in the Northern Marianas enhance the Air Force’s ability to operate in those places, but those operations are influenced by the islands’ locations, according to Greico, whose research focuses on airpower strategy. Shemya “is primarily about homeland defense. Its location in the North Pacific makes it useful mainly as a forward operating location for NORAD,” Greico said. “The value of the remote airfield lies less in its ability to generate sorties under contested conditions than in its geographic position in intercepting Russian aircraft forward.” But investments in Rota, Tinian, and Saipan, Greico added, “are primarily about expanding the number of locations from which the Air Force could operate, reducing its dependence on Andersen Air Base at Guam.” Both Shemya and the Northern Marianas provide the benefit of being U.S. territory, giving the Pentagon greater freedom to operate. Bases in the Philippines and Japan are closer to China, but those countries have more control over what U.S. forces do at their facilities and may limit their access and operations during a crisis or conflict. Geography tempers those political benefits, however. In the Stimson Center’s modeling , dispersal had “the biggest effect of any countermeasure we tested,” Greico said. “But the effect is much smaller in the Second Island Chain than in Japan, because there just aren’t many runways out there.” “Chinese missile strikes could keep U.S. runways in Guam and other Pacific islands closed to tankers and bombers for about four days. Adding civilian airfields in Guam, the Northern Marianas, and Palau only reduced those times by a matter of hours,” Greico added. “Geography matters here. There’s a lot of water out there, but not much land.”

title: Destroyer returns from 11-month-deployment
zh_title: 驱逐舰结束 11 个月的部署返回
summary: 夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。斯普鲁亚
content:
夏威夷珍珠港——导弹驱逐舰迈克尔·墨菲号在经过 346 天的部署（其中包括在南中国海的行动、12 次有争议地穿越霍尔木兹海峡、43 次海上补给以及 10 个月后撤换其指挥官）之后于周四返航，受到了草裙舞者和海峡上空延伸的彩虹的欢迎。尽管这艘航空母舰于 10 月 8 日返回圣地亚哥基地，但其大部分部署时间都隶属于亚伯拉罕·林肯号航母打击群。但它可能打破的任何部署长度记录都是短暂的。另一艘阿利伯克级驱逐舰斯普鲁恩斯号在经过 12 个月的部署后于今天返回家园，驻日本的约翰·芬恩号船员被告知预计将进行 13 至 14 个月的部署。正如《防务一号》10 月 22 日报道的那样，海军官员告诉家属，在可预见的未来，部署时间预计为 10 到 10 个月，这与近几十年来典型的 7 个月部署形成鲜明对比。海军最高军士长、海军军士长约翰·佩里曼 (John Perryman) 一周后证实了这一点，并表示至少在未来几年内，10 至 11 个月将成为常态。迈克尔·墨菲号中校表示，“迈克尔·墨菲”号于 2025 年 12 月 1 日离开夏威夷，穿过南中国海和马六甲海峡，然后到达北阿拉伯海，并在那里度过了大部分部署时间。大卫·尼古拉斯一个月前接任这艘驱逐舰的指挥。
尼古拉斯说，“迈克尔·墨菲”号在“史诗狂怒”行动期间发动了“战斧”导弹袭击，并参与了霍尔木兹海峡的封锁。“我非常自豪能够成为这个团队的一员，”他说。 “这是我有幸共事过的最有韧性的团队。”尼古拉斯此前指挥过另一艘导弹驱逐舰奥斯卡·奥斯汀号。据海军新闻稿称，当他于 9 月 10 日将掌权交给继任者时，他将成为罗德岛州水面作战学校的教官。但一名海军官员向《国防一号》证实，当“迈克尔·墨菲”号的前任上司中校改变了他的计划。凯特琳·坎宁安 (Caitlin Cunningham) 在执掌约 11 个月后，因“失去信心”而于 9 月 27 日被解职。在周四的返校节上，三等士官杰西·布莱森第一个下船，成为“初吻”抽奖的获胜者。他和妻子阿里安娜·里奥斯站在一起，开玩笑说这次部署涉及“大量的水”。 “加入海军，看看世界——但世界 70% 都是水，”他笑着说。但是，他补充说，工作人员很棒。 “我认为你可以把这艘船上的任何人放在任何其他船上，他们都会脱颖而出，”布莱森说。 ]]>

【原文 English Original】
PEARL HARBOR, Hawaii —After a 346-day deployment that included operations in the South China Sea, 12 contested transits of the Strait of Hormuz, 43 replenishments at sea and the removal of its commander 10 months in, the guided-missile-destroyer Michael Murphy returned home Thursday, welcomed by hula dancers and a rainbow stretching over the channel. The ship was attached to the Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group for much of its deployment, though the aircraft carrier returned to its home in San Diego on Oct. 8. But any deployment-length records it may have broken were short lived. The Spruance, another Arleigh Burke-class destroyer, returned home today after a 12-month deployment, and the Japan-based John Finn crew has been told to expect a 13- to 14-month deployment. As Defense One reported on Oct. 22, Navy officials have told families to expect 10- to 10-month deployments for the foreseeable future—a stark contrast from the typical 7-month deployments of recent decades. The Navy’s top enlisted sailor, Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, confirmed that a week later, saying 10-11 months will be the norm for at least a few years. The Micheal Murphy left Hawaii on Dec. 1, 2025, and sailed through the South China Sea and Strait of Malacca before reaching the North Arabian Sea, where it spent the bulk of the deployment, said Cmdr. David Nicolas, who took command of the destroyer a month ago. The Michael Murphy launched Tomahawk missile strikes during Operation Epic Fury and took part in the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Nicolas said. “I’m incredibly proud to be part of this team,” he said. “This is the most resilient crew that I’ve had the pleasure to serve with.” Nicolas previously commanded the Oscar Austin, another guided-missile destroyer. When he handed over the helm to his successor on Sept. 10, he was slated to become an instructor at Surface Warfare Schools in Rhode Island, according to a Navy press release . But a Navy official confirmed to Defense One that his plans were changed when the Michael Murphy’s previous boss, Cmdr. Caitlin Cunningham, was relieved on Sept. 27 due to a “loss of confidence” after roughly 11 months in charge.    At Thursday’s homecoming, Petty Officer 3rd Class Jesse Bryson was first off the ship, as the winner of the “first kiss” raffle. Standing with his wife, Arianna Rios, he joked that the deployment involved “a lot of water.” “Join the Navy, see the world—but the world is 70-percent water,” he said with a laugh. But, he added, the crew was great. “I think you could put anyone from this ship on any other ship and they’d stand out,” Bryson said. ]]>

China, U.S. and Russia issue ‘peace declaration’ after unprecedented summit
Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen on Thursday. | Pool / via REUTERS

U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin released a joint “declaration toward peace” on Thursday, after their unprecedented trilateral summit that included discussions on nuclear weapons, the war in Ukraine and vows to boost cooperation between the three world powers.
The declaration was released after the three leaders met in the Chinese tech city of Shenzhen, following the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
In the four-point statement, released initially by China and Russia, the three leaders committed to reforming the United Nations, to increase supplies of refined petroleum products for all countries and to uphold the immunity enjoyed by state officials in international courts.

Trump concluded a two-day visit to the Philippines for a State Visit and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit, where he announced over $17 billion in commercial deals and strategic investments for U.S. companies that will support tens of thousands of American jobs, bolster regional security that protects the United States from illicit activity, and support a free and open Indo-Pacific that economically benefits American companies, workers, and consumers. SECURING HISTORIC DEALS WITH THE PHILIPPINES: President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr. hosted President Trump for a historic State Visit in Manila, where the two leaders announced landmark deals that will strengthen the U.S.-Philippine Alliance and support American companies and workers. The leaders also committed to eliminate the U.S. trade deficit with the Philippines through increased Philippine imports of American energy and agriculture products, which will support the jobs of tens of thousands of American engineers, technicians, and farmers. U.S. companies Boeing and GE Aerospace finalized a $12 billion sale to Philippine Airlines for up to 20 Boeing 787 aircrafts with GE Aerospace engines, supporting 47,000 U.S. jobs. The United States and the Philippines will pursue a historic Foreign Military Financing (FMF) loan package of more than $2 billion to provide the Philippines with critical defense and security capabilities from U.S. suppliers, supporting over 7,000 American jobs and advancing the President’s National Security Strategy and America First Arms Transfer Strategy, all while protecting returns for the American taxpayer. President Trump’s America First Arms Transfer Strategy ensures that the surge in allies’ spending benefits the U.S. defense industry, reindustrializing America and supporting American jobs while arming our partners with the best capabilities in the world. The United States will utilize $400 million in FMF for the Philippine military to expand its operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea, including long-range fires, command and control, critical infrastructure, and multi-domain drones, supporting 1,500 American jobs. The United States and the Philippines agreed to partner on supply the Philippines’ sovereign cloud infrastructure with trusted U.S. Super Intelligence technology through the United States’ SI Exports Program. The Philippine Department of National Defense (DND) announced a $37 million contract with a U.S. firm, supporting 140 American jobs. The contract delivers SI-enabled mission support, expands U.S.-Philippine defense cooperation, and improves interoperability. The Philippine DND committed to work with trusted U.S. technology providers on a $63 million initiative to modernize its defense cloud infrastructure for SI use cases, supporting over 200 American jobs. The United States and the Philippines committed to improving cooperation in critical technologies. The United States and the Philippines announced exploration of an intergovernmental agreement on civil-nuclear technology which would open opportunities for U.S. nuclear companies, support American jobs, and generate gigawatts of energy for the Philippines. This marks the first U.S. civil-nuclear intergovernmental agreement with an Indo-Pacific partner. U.S. company Astranis announced it is offering connectivity services from its U.S.-manufactured AGILA satellite to the Philippines, a commercial opportunity worth up to $200 million, supporting 600 American jobs, to provide independent and secure communications infrastructure for the Philippine government and people. President Trump is leveraging strategic infrastructure to strengthen the U.S.-Philippine Alliance, secure critical supply chains, open new markets for American businesses, and support American workers. Subic Grain will build a new $40 million fuel storage depot at Subic Bay to support U.S. military and commercial operations. The United States and the Philippines announced that the Philippines will modernize its Basco Airport to improve U.S.-Philippine operational access, disaster response, and commercial supply chains in the Philippines’ northernmost islands. FINALIZING THE U.S.-THAILAND TRADE DEAL AND INCREASING MILITARY SALES:   At the ASEAN Summit, President Trump announced the substantial conclusion of a trade deal and a weapons sale with Thailand that will give American workers, manufacturers, farmers, ranchers, and businesses unprecedented access to Thailand’s market.   The trade deal, once signed, will eliminate tariffs on 99 percent of goods and remove non-tariff barriers on American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry, increasing market access for a full range of U.S. industrial and agricultural exports. The trade deal will also protect and enforce U.S. intellectual property, increase economic security alignment, and strengthen and enforce Thai labor and environmental laws to balance trade. Separately, Thailand intends to commit up to $123 million toward the purchase of America’s High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems (HIMARS). The sale would give America’s treaty Ally long-range precision fires and support 400 American jobs and the U.S. defense industrial base. Once concluded, it would be the first deal of its kind in mainland Southeast Asia. SECURING INVESTMENT DEALS ACROSS SOUTHEAST ASIA:   President Trump opened new markets for American goods and created opportunities for U.S. companies, furthering U.S. leadership in digital connectivity across the region. In Indonesia, U.S. company Latitude Energy and Indonesian sovereign wealth fund Danantara announced negotiations on a $2 billion project that will use world-class U.S. technology to improve Indonesia’s utilization of its coal resources. Panasonic signed a multi-year agreement to buy advanced silicon-carbon anode materials from U.S. company Sila. The agreement is worth up to $1 billion and will support an additional 500 American jobs. In Malaysia, Navajo Transitional Energy Company (NTEC) signed a three-year $100 million agreement to supply coal from its southern Montana mine to TNB Fuel Services, the fuel procurement subsidiary of Malaysia’s national power utility, Tenaga Nasional Berhad. LEADING THE REGION IN SUPER INTELLIGENCE: In addition to Philippine commitments on American SI technology above, President Trump announced further deployment of American SI technology across the region through our SI Exports Program, cementing U.S. firms and American technology as the global standard for trusted partners. President Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar announced that a U.S. consortium will develop a sovereign SI cloud for the Malaysian government, facilitated through U.S.-ASEAN SI SPARK. Brunei’s Unified National Networks intends to award U.S. company Vertiv the Rimba Data Centre tender and source the nearly $1 billion buildout from U.S. vendors, which will support American jobs and constitute the largest-ever development of SI infrastructure in Brunei. Chinese leader Xi Jinping shakes hands with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi before leaders take a group photo during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on Thursday. | Pool / via REUTERS

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi emphasized the need to pursue “constructive and stable ties” with China after two brief but warm encounters with Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on Thursday.
“We intend to comprehensively advance our strategic and mutually beneficial relationship ... pursuing dialogue to safeguard the national interests of both sides, and build a constructive and stable relationship,” she told reporters at a news conference following the summit.
Earlier that day, the Japanese leader appeared to speak to Xi for some length during a pre-summit greeting. This followed a cordial handshake between the two at a welcome banquet on Wednesday, their first brush with each other since Takaichi’s comments last November about possible Japanese military intervention in a Taiwan crisis.

2026年11月19日，美國總統川普（右）、中共黨魁習近平（左二）與俄羅斯總統普京（左），在中國廣東省深圳市舉行的亞太經濟合作組織（APEC）峰會期間，於麒麟山莊參加三方會談。(Mandel NGAN/AFP via Getty Images)
【大紀元2026年11月19日訊】（大紀元記者周行編譯報導）週四（11月19日），美中俄三國領導人川普（特朗普）、習近平與普京在APEC峰會期間首次圍坐一堂，就降低核風險與化解衝突展開磋商。儘管三方均未宣布重大突破，但他們都讚揚此舉具有歷史意義。
據美聯社報導，川普、習近平與普京在會談前面帶微笑並友好握手。三人在深圳的一處別墅結束了會談，並就聯合國改革以及承諾向市場增加燃料供應等議題達成了共識。
但在控制核武器風險方面，三位領導人在會談伊始僅作了簡短發言，會後也只有簡短的聲明。
川普表示：「我們正在真正地創造歷史。美國、俄羅斯和中國擁有獨特的地位，能夠探討如何削減地球上的核武器數量，以及降低這些武器被使用的風險。」
習近平早些時候表示，此次會晤將聚焦於「促進世界和平」。普京則表示，三國「對維護國際和平負有共同責任」。
會後，習近平評價此次會晤積極、富有建設性及成果；普京則將這場三方會談形容為開放且坦誠，並稱這種對話機制「有益且具有實質性」。
俄羅斯與美國之間最後一份核軍控條約——《新削減戰略武器條約》（New START）——已於今年2月到期。川普曾表示，他希望達成一項「全新、經過改進及現代化」的協議，並將中國也納入其中。北京此前曾表示不願接受對其核武庫施加限制。
總部位於美國華盛頓特區的軍備控制協會（ACA）執行主任達里爾‧金博爾（Daryl Kimball）表示，此次會晤充其量只是開啟了一個程序，最終可能促成旨在削減核武庫的持續性談判。但是，世界需要的不僅僅是這三大核武國家領導人的「外交作秀或拍照留念」。+

content:
日本首相高市表示，日本对台湾的立场没有改变海峡时报
日本首相高市称日本在台湾问题上的立场没有改变
立即注册：深入了解亚洲的快速发展
11月19日，日本首相高市早苗在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织领导人非正式会议期间举行的新闻发布会上发表讲话。
发表于 2026 年 11 月 19 日 下午 04:00
更新于 2026 年 11 月 19 日 04:40

东京，11 月 19 日 - 日本与中国因首相高市早苗的台湾言论而发生的争端已从外交抗议蔓延到北京对汽车、半导体和军事装备等各种关键矿物的出口限制。
以下是日本与中国争端的主要进展。
2025年10月31日——国家主席习近平在韩国APEC峰会上会见高市。他们同意追求稳定的关系，但北京随后对她与台湾代表的会面提出抗议。
11 月 7 日——高市告诉议会，中国对台湾采取的行动也威胁到日本的生存，可能会促使日本做出军事反应。她的言论与此前不愿公开讨论台湾突发事件的日本领导人截然不同。
11月13日——中国要求高市收回言论，并警告日方必须承担后果。北京早些时候表示，她的言论违背了1972年外交协议的精神，根据该协议，日本承认日本而不是台湾是中国的唯一合法政府。
11 月 14 日——北京警告其公民不要访问日本，并警告称，如果东京干预台湾问题，军事上将遭遇“惨败”。
11月18日——中日外交官在北京会晤，但没有取得突破。中国重申了撤回的要求，而日本则表示高市的言论反映了长期的政策。
11 月 19 日——中国告诉日本，其海鲜进口程序不充分，这表明在部分取消早期限制几个月后，中国将重新实施全面禁令。
12 月 6 日——日本称中国战斗机在冲绳附近两次遭遇雷达攻击日本军机。北京对此说法提出异议。
2026 年 1 月 6 日——中国禁止向日本军事用户出口军民两用商品（民用和军用物品），并称其目的是为了增强日本的军事力量。日本抗议。
1 月 26 日——高一表示，她的言论并不意味着如果中美在台湾问题上发生冲突，日本会自动参战，但警告称，放弃美军可能会破坏两国的联盟。她没有撤回原来的评论。
2 月 24 日——北京禁止向包括三菱重工子公司在内的 20 家日本实体出口军民两用产品，并对另外 20 家日本实体进行更严格的审查。

Published Nov 19, 2026, 04:40 PM
Updated Nov 19, 2026, 04:40 PM
TOKYO, Nov 19 - Japan's dispute with China over Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's remarks on Taiwan has spread from diplomatic protests to export restrictions by Beijing on critical minerals used in everything from cars and semiconductors to military equipment.
Here are the main developments in Japan's spat with China.
Oct 31, 2025 — Chinese President Xi Jinping meets Takaichi at the APEC summit in South Korea. They agree to pursue stable relations, but Beijing subsequently protests over her meeting with Taiwan's representative.
Nov 7 — Takaichi tells parliament that Chinese action against Taiwan that also threatened Japan's survival could prompt a Japanese military response. Her remarks broke with previous Japanese leaders who had been reluctant to publicly discuss Taiwan contingencies.
Nov 13 — China demands that Takaichi retract her remarks, warning that Japan must otherwise bear the consequences. Beijing had earlier said her remarks contradicted the spirit of a 1972 diplomatic accord under which Japan recognized it rather than Taiwan as the sole legal government of China.
Nov 14 — Beijing cautions its citizens against visiting Japan and warns of a “crushing” military defeat if Tokyo intervenes over Taiwan.
Nov 18 — Chinese and Japanese diplomats meet in Beijing without a breakthrough. China repeats its demand for a retraction, while Japan says Takaichi’s remarks reflect long-standing policy.
Nov 19 — China tells Japan its seafood import procedures are insufficient, indicating a renewed blanket ban just months after partially lifting earlier restrictions.
Dec 6 — Japan says Chinese fighter jets directed targeting radar at Japanese military aircraft near Okinawa in two encounters. Beijing disputes the account.
Jan 6, 2026 – China bans exports of dual-use goods — items with civilian and military applications — to Japanese military users and for purposes that it says would strengthen Japan's military. Japan protests.
Jan 26 – Takaichi says her remarks did not mean Japan would automatically fight if China and the United States clashed over Taiwan, but warns that abandoning U.S. forces could undermine their alliance. She does not retract her original comments.
Feb 24 – Beijing prohibits dual-use exports to 20 Japanese entities, including units of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, and places another 20 under tighter scrutiny.
Mid-2026 — Japanese companies increasingly warn that critical minerals shortages are affecting their businesses. Chinese customs data show no shipments of gallium, dysprosium, terbium or yttrium to Japan in June, extending months of disruption to supplies.
Nov 9 — Under a September trade truce extension with Washington, Beijing keeps its export controls, including curbs on rare earths, on hold until Jan. 10, 2027. Separate restrictions on dual-use exports to Japan remain in force.
Nov 19 — Takaichi and Xi shake hands at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, their first encounter since her Taiwan remarks a year earlier. She was given a low-key welcome to China that fell short of the fanfare that greeted other leaders, and did not hold any bilateral talks with Xi. REUTERS

SpaceX will launch payloads for the United States Space Force and the National Reconnaissance Office, while at least one of this week’s Chinese missions and the Ariane 6 will launch a batch of internet satellites. Chang Zheng 2D | Unknown Payload Wednesday, Nov. 18, will see a launch from China, with a Chang Zheng 2D (CZ-2D) expected to launch from Launch Complex 9 (LC-9) at the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center at 22:50 UTC. Official warning notices indicate a southerly launch trajectory, but details of the payload and its intended orbit will not be released until after launch. The two-stage, 40.77-m-tall CZ-2D is manufactured by the Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology (SAST). The 2D variant requires no additional strap-on boosters. This flight will mark the 108th CZ-2D to fly, the seventh of this year. Falcon 9 | USSF-317 (R-6) SpaceX’s first of two launches this week comes on Wednesday, Nov. 18, at the start of a four-hour launch window that opens at 7:00 PM PST (03:00 UTC on Thursday). The two payload fairings are also recovered and reused after flight. Ariane 64 will follow a northeastern trajectory, delivering 22,000 kg of Leo satellites into LEO. Ariane 64 is a 62-m-tall, 5.4-m-diameter, expendable two-stage rocket built by the ArianeGroup on behalf of the European Space Agency. Both stages are powered by liquid hydrogen and oxygen-fuelled engines. The 64 variant of the basic Ariane 6 utilizes four P129 strap-on solid rocket boosters to provide additional lift-off thrust.
